principles: Must-always-run covers repository/build/unit/deterministic authoritative contracts plus the current checkpoint's 90-variant track-aware movement/acquisition study.
Deep Calibration remains opt-in unless a checkpoint changes accepted combat mechanics broadly enough to require historical stochastic requalification.

The accepted Checkpoint 63b 72-variant operational sensor study, Checkpoint 62 108-variant power-doctrine/reactor study, and Checkpoint 61 54-variant composed-build study move to Deep Calibration as historical stochastic regression evidence.
Production TL1 reactor output remains 5 Tactical Power and FullVolleyFirst remains fixed so power-allocation and reactor-output changes do not confound the movement/acquisition question.
TrackAwareOpponentRange caps weapon standoff by the Firm range the ship can support while preserving its ready volley when possible; it does not guarantee closure against an equal-or-faster opponent.
AcquisitionFirstAutoActive may spend the minimum active-sensor power needed for Firm after movement before PDS allocation, even when fewer ready weapons can then fire.
All cruisers retain core passive/navigation sensing and sensorless builds may never synthesize active-sensor power.
Side B retains an established Firm solution; EW1 remains an abstract one-hex net range-pressure stress input.
Simulation diagnoses consequences; it does not manufacture fixed build or weapon-family win percentages.
Latent/contextual advantages remain valid design value when the current opponent does not exercise them; Energy APEN remains the explicit standing example.
Generated historical checkpoint text logs/manifests/readmes remain excluded from full-repository packaging unless active tooling explicitly consumes them.

notes.reasonDeepCalibrationNotRequired: The new movement mode and acquisition-first track policy are opt-in fields used only by the Checkpoint 64 study. Accepted historical variants retain OpponentAwareRange and their prior track policies.
